KO.rationale: Coca-Cola delivered a strong Q2 2026 with revenue of $13.38B (+7% YoY), adjusted EPS of $0.97 beating consensus of $0.93, and raised full-year guidance to 9-10% EPS growth and ~5% organic revenue growth. The company's asset-light concentrate model continues to generate high margins (35.6% comparable operating margin) and strong cash flows, with a 64-year dividend increase streak reinforcing its defensive franchise. However, the stock is trading near all-time highs at a P/E of ~27.7x, which is at the upper end of its 1-year range (23.2-31.2x) and represents a premium for a company with mid-single-digit organic growth. The IRS tax dispute with ~$14B potential exposure is a material overhang, and the fairlife ransomware incident adds operational risk. While the Q2 beat and guidance raise provide a near-term positive catalyst, the elevated valuation limits upside from here, making the risk-reward balanced rather than compelling.
key_factors: Strong Q2 2026 results: revenue $13.38B (+7% YoY), adjusted EPS $0.97 vs consensus $0.93, raised full-year guidance to 9-10% EPS growth
Asset-light concentrate model with 35.6% comparable operating margin and 64-year dividend increase streak
Stock trading near all-time highs at P/E ~27.7x, at upper end of 1-year range (23.2-31.2x), premium for mid-single-digit growth
IRS tax dispute with ~$14B potential aggregate exposure for 2010-2025 is a material overhang
Fairlife ransomware incident (July 16, 2026) temporarily suspended US production, adding operational risk
World Cup marketing drove 5% unit case volume growth, strongest Coca-Cola trademark quarter in 17 years ex-COVID
Global value share gains in NARTD beverages across most segments

sources_cited.excerpt: Adjusted earnings per share: 97 cents, vs. expected 93 cents; Revenue: $13.38 billion, vs. $13.16 billion expected. Coke is now projecting comparable earnings per share growth of 9% to 10%, up from its prior forecast of 8% to 9%.
Net income reached $4,425M on Q2 2026 revenue of $13,380M. Coca-Cola also details an estimated $14B potential tax exposure from its long-running IRS dispute.

On July 16, 2026, The Coca-Cola Company disclosed that its dairy subsidiary fairlife, LLC had identified unauthorized access by a third party to a portion of its systems, including production-related systems, in connection with a ransomware event. US production operations at fairlife were temporarily suspended.
Global Unit Case Volume Grew 5%. Comparable Operating Margin (Non-GAAP) was 35.6% versus 34.7% in the Prior Year. The company gained value share in total nonalcoholic ready-to-drink beverages.
